```{r}
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  candidate <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  repeat {
    if (file.exists(file.path(candidate, "renv.lock"))) return(candidate)
    parent <- dirname(candidate)
    if (identical(parent, candidate)) {
      stop("Could not locate the project root", call. = FALSE)
    }
    candidate <- parent
  }
}

artifact <- function(stage, file) {
  file.path(project_root, "artifacts", stage, "H06_daily", file)
}
read_h06d <- function(stage, file) {
  readr::read_csv(
    artifact(stage, file),
    show_col_types = FALSE,
    na = c("", "NA")
  )
}
sha256 <- function(path) digest::digest(path, algo = "sha256", file = TRUE)
verify_relative_manifest <- function(manifest, hash_column = "sha256") {
  paths <- file.path(project_root, manifest$relative_path)
  stopifnot(all(file.exists(paths)))
  actual <- unname(vapply(paths, sha256, character(1)))
  stopifnot(identical(actual, manifest[[hash_column]]))
  invisible(TRUE)
}
compact_gt <- function(table, source_note = NULL) {
  output <- table |>
    gt::gt() |>
    gt::tab_options(
      table.font.size = gt::px(12),
      data_row.padding = gt::px(3),
      heading.padding = gt::px(4),
      column_labels.padding = gt::px(4),
      table.width = gt::pct(100),
      source_notes.font.size = gt::px(11),
      row_group.padding = gt::px(4)
    )
  if (!is.null(source_note)) {
    output <- output |> gt::tab_source_note(gt::md(source_note))
  }
  output
}
format_p <- function(value) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(value) ~ "—",
    value < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
    TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", value)
  )
}
`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (length(x) == 0L || is.na(x)) y else x
format_effect <- function(estimate, lower, upper, scale) {
  digits <- ifelse(grepl("^ratio", scale), 3L, 2L)
  ifelse(
    is.na(estimate),
    "—",
    sprintf(
      paste0("%.", digits, "f (%.", digits, "f to %.", digits, "f)"),
      estimate,
      lower,
      upper
    )
  )
}
short_status <- function(value) {
  dplyr::recode(
    value,
    ACCEPTABLE = "Acceptable",
    ACCEPTABLE_WITH_LIMITATION = "Acceptable with limitation",
    NOT_ACCEPTABLE = "Not acceptable",
    .default = value
  )
}
```

# Stage 2 verdict

::: {.callout-important title="H06-D-G2 status — author review required"}

The authorized production grid is complete: **468** non-L10 metric × predictor
× scenario cells, **936** raw omnibus tests, **66,664** participant/site
deletion refits, and **12 complete named 15-slot Benjamini--Hochberg (BH)
families**. L10 mean remains the frozen named non-estimable slot 3; MDER raw
results remain frozen in slot 15, with only its mathematically dependent BH
fields recalculated.

Of the 39 primary near-eye non-L10 cells,
`r primary_diagnostic_counts$cells[match("ACCEPTABLE", primary_diagnostic_counts$diagnostic_status)] %||% 0`
are acceptable,
`r primary_diagnostic_counts$cells[match("ACCEPTABLE_WITH_LIMITATION", primary_diagnostic_counts$diagnostic_status)] %||% 0`
are acceptable only with an explicit limitation, and
`r primary_diagnostic_counts$cells[match("NOT_ACCEPTABLE", primary_diagnostic_counts$diagnostic_status)] %||% 0`
do not support an unqualified association claim under the prespecified rules.
The individual estimates and complete multiplicity vectors remain visible
below so numerical results are not selected after diagnostics.

This document is the mandatory Stage 2 stop. It does **not** authorize the
compact Stage 3 reader report, the separate Stage 4 provenance companion,
website integration, or any change to the selected hourly main H06 analysis.

:::

# Scientific target and analysis roles

The daily variant asks how recorded day-level contexts are associated with
participant-day light-exposure metrics. Each admissible metric-specific day
contributes exactly one row. It neither models repeated hourly melEDI nor
weights days by the number of supported hours. Under `H06-007`, the completed
hourly H06 analysis remains the main analysis; this daily analysis is
complementary evidence closer to the registered daily-metric outcome wording.

# Exact production implementation

## Model routes

The nine non-timing outcomes retain the approved fixed-site mixed-model
hierarchy, with a participant random intercept:

```r
response_value ~ site + (1 | participant_key)
response_value ~ site + predictor + (1 | participant_key)
response_value ~ site * predictor + (1 | participant_key)
```

Gaussian comparisons use maximum likelihood and estimates use REML. Tweedie
models use a log link. The registered random-site/random-slope formula remains
a visible benchmark and never replaces the fixed-site primary hierarchy.

The four repaired timing outcomes use the uniformly accepted fixed-site linear
hierarchy:

```r
response_value ~ site
response_value ~ site + predictor
response_value ~ site * predictor
```

Their covariance is participant-cluster HC3 from
`sandwich::vcovCL(type = "HC3", cadjust = TRUE, fix = FALSE)`, with
participant-cluster-minus-one t/F references and **pointwise** 95% confidence
intervals. No simultaneous interval is used.

Site uses sum-to-zero coding throughout. Categorical effects are Free day
minus Work day and Active minus Sedentary. Sleep duration is the per-hour
association for a previous-night duration centered at 8 h. Because this daily
model does not include separate participant-mean and day-deviation sleep terms,
that coefficient combines between-participant and within-participant
comparisons; the participant random intercept does not by itself separate
them. Equal-site marginalization is used rather than weighting sites by their
number of observations.

# Primary near-eye estimates

The two figures show adjusted effects and pointwise 95% confidence intervals.
Ratios refer to the fitted response scale stated in the source table—for
shifted-log outcomes, the ratio is for the fitted metric plus 0.1, not a raw
metric ratio. Absolute timing and duration effects are shown in hours.

## L10 and MDER dispositions

L10 mean melEDI remains `NON_ESTIMABLE_COMPONENT_FAILURE` in all 12 joint
slots; its raw and adjusted p-values are missing. Positive-only and MAP results
remain descriptive historical diagnostics and are not substituted. MDER uses
the approved arithmetic mean of viable positive finite one-minute
melEDI/illuminance ratios. Its raw model results are frozen; only family-wide
adjusted fields change when the 15-slot vectors are completed.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-frozen-slots
#| tbl-cap: "Primary association-family status for frozen slots 3 and 15."

families |>
  dplyr::filter(
    .data$dataset_id == "primary",
    .data$test_type == "association",
    .data$metric_slot %in% c(3L, 15L)
  ) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Predictor = .data$reader_name,
    Slot = .data$metric_slot,
    Metric = .data$manuscript_name,
    `Slot status` = .data$slot_status,
    `Raw p` = format_p(.data$raw_p_value),
    `BH q` = format_p(.data$bh_adjusted_p_value),
    `Adjusted decision` = .data$adjusted_inferential_decision
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste0(
      "No L10 or MDER model, estimate, interval, diagnostic, sensitivity, or raw ",
      "p-value was refitted or changed in this production run."
    )
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = Slot)
```

The selected-candidate MDER point estimates and pointwise 95% intervals are
retained below for context; they remain the sealed METRIC-010 results.

```{r}
    .data$sensitivity_role == "selected candidate"
  ) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Predictor = .data$predictor,
    Contrast = .data$contrast,
    `Participant-days` = .data$participant_days,
    Participants = .data$participants,
    `MDER difference (95% CI)` = sprintf(
      "%.3f (%.3f to %.3f)",
      .data$estimate,
      .data$lower_95,
      .data$upper_95
    )
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste0(
      "Absolute MDER differences from the frozen Gaussian selected candidate. ",
      "Student-t sensitivities remain stored separately."
    )
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = c(`Participant-days`, Participants))
```

## All 468 cells


The detailed assessment preserves model, distribution, temporal, continuous-
period, and influence gates separately. The primary near-eye cells are shown
below.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-primary-diagnostics
#| tbl-cap: "Primary near-eye diagnostic assessments by metric and predictor."

diagnostics |>
  dplyr::filter(
    .data$dataset_id == "primary",
    .data$placement_id == "near_eye",
    .data$sample_role == "all_available"
  ) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Slot = .data$metric_slot,
    Metric = .data$manuscript_name,
    Predictor = .data$reader_name,
    Model = dplyr::case_when(
      startsWith(.data$model_gate, "ACCEPTABLE_WITH") ~ "Limit",
      startsWith(.data$model_gate, "ACCEPTABLE") ~ "OK",
      TRUE ~ "No"
    ),
    Distribution = dplyr::case_when(
      startsWith(.data$distribution_gate, "ACCEPTABLE_WITH") ~ "Limit",
      startsWith(.data$distribution_gate, "ACCEPTABLE") ~ "OK",
      TRUE ~ "No"
    ),
    Temporal = dplyr::case_when(
      startsWith(.data$temporal_gate, "ACCEPTABLE_WITH") ~ "Limit",
      startsWith(.data$temporal_gate, "ACCEPTABLE") ~ "OK",
      TRUE ~ "No"
    ),
    Period = dplyr::case_when(
      startsWith(.data$period_gate, "ACCEPTABLE_WITH") ~ "Limit",
      startsWith(.data$period_gate, "ACCEPTABLE") ~ "OK",
      TRUE ~ "No"
    ),
    Influence = dplyr::case_when(
      startsWith(.data$influence_gate, "ACCEPTABLE_WITH") ~ "Limit",
      startsWith(.data$influence_gate, "ACCEPTABLE") ~ "OK",
      TRUE ~ "No"
    ),
    Overall = dplyr::case_when(
      .data$diagnostic_status == "ACCEPTABLE_WITH_LIMITATION" ~ "Limit",
      .data$diagnostic_status == "ACCEPTABLE" ~ "OK",
      TRUE ~ "No"
    )
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste0(
      "OK = acceptable; Limit = acceptable only with the stated limitation; ",
      "No = not acceptable. Full diagnostic codes are in the paired production CSV. ",
      "H06-D-011 timing qualifications remain binding even when a raw test is small."
    )
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = Slot) |>
  gt::cols_width(
    Slot ~ gt::px(38),
    Metric ~ gt::px(170),
    Predictor ~ gt::px(110),
    c(Model, Distribution, Temporal, Period, Influence, Overall) ~ gt::px(72)
  ) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = gt::px(9))
```

## Temporal dependence and timing-route qualifications

The accepted timing route retains all earlier limitations. In particular,
first timing above 250 lx melEDI for Work versus Free day had a 1.23-HC3-SE
Student-t shift; L10 midpoint activity had a 1.26-HC3-SE no-nugget AR shift;
three pilot additive AR fits were unresolved; no pilot AR structure met the
pooled-and-every-site lag rule; and timing site interactions remain
sensitivity-dependent. Production significance cannot erase these facts.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-temporal-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Temporal-stability dispositions in the complete production grid."

mixed_temporal <- diagnostics |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$route == "mixed_model") |>
  dplyr::count(
    Route = "Mixed-model outcomes",
    Disposition = .data$temporal_gate,
    name = "Cells"
  )
timing_temporal <- diagnostics |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$route == "participant_cluster_HC3") |>
  dplyr::count(
    Route = "Participant-cluster HC3 timing outcomes",
    Disposition = .data$temporal_gate,
    name = "Cells"
  )
dplyr::bind_rows(mixed_temporal, timing_temporal) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste0(
      "AR counterparts are diagnostic sensitivities and never replace the ",
      "approved primary route or its raw p-value."
    )
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = Cells)
```

# Comparison with V0

## Implementation-level comparison

| Component | V0 implementation | Current H06 daily implementation | Claim consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outcome | Repeated hourly geometric-mean melEDI | Fifteen distinct participant-day metrics | Different estimands; no hourly coefficient transfers |
| Formula | `geo.MEDI ~ site*daytype + site*exercise + site*sleep_duration + (1|Id)` | Separate reduced/additive/site-interaction hierarchy for each metric and predictor | No V0 coefficient maps one-to-one to a daily-metric result |
| Predictor encoding | Free/work, four-level exercise intensity, and sleep duration jointly | Work/Free day, day-level Active/Sedentary status, and within-person previous-night sleep duration separately | Predictor meaning and adjustment differ |
| Day weighting | One row per retained hour | One row per admissible metric-specific participant-day | Days are not weighted by supported-hour count |
| Dependence | Participant intercept only | Participant intercept or participant-cluster HC3, plus the prespecified actual-date temporal screen | Uncertainty and diagnostic acceptance differ |
| Site | Fixed interactions with a stale displayed site p-value | Equal-site fixed-site association plus a separate heterogeneity test; registered benchmark visible | Site evidence is reconstructed rather than copied |
| Multiplicity | Raw predictor-block p-values labelled as FDR | Twelve named 15-slot BH vectors | V0 significance labels are not retained |
| Uncertainty | Final table omitted 95% intervals | Pointwise 95% intervals for every estimable effect | Magnitude and uncertainty are explicit |
| Placement | Signed chest primary but near-eye-focused reporting | Near eye primary; chest and paired/common complementary | Placement roles are transparent |

## Claim-level disposition

V0 hourly ratios, site contrasts, and “unique variance” fractions remain
historical descriptors. They cannot be restated as effects on daily mean,
M10/L10, threshold durations, exposure timing, melEDI dose, MDER, or the
longest continuous period. This Stage 2 analysis supports only metric-specific
observational statements on its own exact frames and only where the declared
diagnostic status permits them. Numerical similarity between hourly and daily
results is neither expected nor an equivalence test.

```{r}

runtime |>
  dplyr::mutate(

      .data$wall_seconds < 60,

    Execution = .data$execution
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste0(

  ) |>

```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-software
#| tbl-cap: "Authoritative production software identities."

software_manifest |>
  dplyr::select(Item = .data$item, Version = .data$version, Role = .data$role) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste0(
```

The input manifest contains `r nrow(input_manifest)` sealed identities; the
scientific-output manifest contains `r nrow(output_manifest)` identities; the
figure manifest pairs two publication-scale figures with two source-data CSVs;
and the final preservation audit confirms `r nrow(preservation)` protected
historical H06_daily and main-H06 files byte-for-byte.

The current prepared metrics retain the PREP06-BASE-002 qualification:
state-support reconstruction inherits the bounded PREP-003/FIND-044 provenance
limitation. This qualification is not evidence that the current metric values
are analytically wrong.

# H06-D-G2 author decisions

::: {.callout-important title="Stop gate — explicit Stage 2 approval required"}

Please approve or amend all of the following before any Stage 3 work:

1. Accept the completed 468-cell production grid, exact samples, model routes,
   and pointwise 95% intervals as the Stage 2 implementation record.
2. Accept the twelve complete named 15-slot BH families, with L10 retained as
   the frozen NA slot and MDER raw/model outputs frozen.
3. Accept the explicit cell-level diagnostic verdicts, including every
   not-acceptable result and major limitation; no small p-value overrides a
   failed diagnostic.
4. Accept the chest, paired/common, and gap-timing-unaware results in their
   declared complementary or sensitivity roles.
5. Retain the completed hourly H06 analysis as the main H06 result and this
   daily analysis as complementary preregistration-oriented evidence.
6. Decide separately whether to authorize Stage 3: a compact standalone
   reader-facing `notebooks/hypotheses/H06_daily.qmd`. Stage 4 remains blocked
   until that Stage 3 report is itself approved.

No model refit, deletion batch, multiplicity change, Stage 3/4 authoring,
website integration, shared edit, main-H06 change, commit, or push follows
automatically from this gate.

:::
